summary: This instructional video is a detailed, field-to-post workflow focused on twilight desert imagery featuring cacti and distant mountains. The presenter demonstrates a zone-based approach to RAW/Photoshop processing, starting with a crop and then isolating sky, middle ground, and foreground highlights to balance exposure. Core techniques include dynamic-range expansion with whites and shadows, careful color shifts, and selective-color work to illuminate cactus glow; a custom sky gradient and vignette are painted in, followed by horizon-focused lighting created with dodge/burn, luminosity, and iterative color grading. He then walks through horizon emphasis, dehazing caveats, and the deliberate use of Gaussian blur separations to push background planes back, culminating in sky replacement via clone-stamping and careful edge handling. The video also touches on focus-stacking notes, field planning (vertical vs. horizontal crops), and the nuanced use of tools like the history brush, clone stamp, content-aware fill, and selective-color (50-150) to sculpt mood and guide viewer attention toward the light source. Throughout, the emphasis is on building a narrative through light paths, composition decisions, and iterative, non-destructive edits with a strong preference for preserving color integrity while revealing hidden shadow detail.

sections.title: Intro and crop-focused workflow
sections.description: Opening remarks set the scene for twilight cactus shots and introduce cropping as the first step. The presenter begins to break the image into zones and notes the importance of cropping first to simplify the composition.

sections.title: Zone-based editing and midtone adjustments
sections.description: The shot is split into sky, middle ground, and cactus-highlight zones. The middle ground is selectively expanded for dynamic range, with exposure and whites refined and a color shift applied to minimize unintended hue shifts.

sections.title: Sky adjustments and vignette technique
sections.description: A custom gradient is applied to desaturate the sky; color balance and a subtle vignette are painted in with the history brush to guide attention toward the horizon.

sections.title: Return to RAW for middle-ground lift
sections.description: Back in RAW, the middle-ground whites are dialed in with a light color-grade tweak to refine the focal area without overpowering the overall palette.

sections.title: Selective color and cactus glow
sections.description: The instructor uses whites with selective color to add warmth to the cactus light. He paints in glow selectively, explaining how this avoids affecting nearby foliage and maintains a cohesive look.

sections.title: Horizon emphasis and sky coloration strategy
sections.description: Further refinements push the horizon as a focal point. Dodge/burn and selective color are used to create a subtle glow, with dehaze noted as a tool that can be risky if overused.

sections.title: Simulated light source and structured glow steps
sections.description: A structured, four-step approach to simulate a light source: haze/contrast handling, luminosity adjustments, color grading, and then re-applying the combined effect to emphasize the light path.

sections.title: 50-150 selective color and background separation
sections.description: The presenter demonstrates selective color at the 50-150 level to intensify warm light on red rocks and to push depth cues, while maintaining separation between background mountains and the foreground via controlled luminosity.

sections.title: Sky replacement and depth layering with edge care
sections.description: Sky blending is tackled with the clone stamp and careful layer separation. Gaussian blur is used to push background mountains back, and edge handling is emphasized to avoid obvious seams. Horizon integrity is preserved by limiting changes to high regions and avoiding horizon distortion.

sections.title: Workflow discipline and field-to-PS strategy
sections.description: The presenter stresses field planning for composition, discusses vertical vs horizontal crops, and explains how in-camera decisions (like light direction and sky presence) influence post-processing choices. He also notes challenges with card transfers and file management during a long editing session.

sections.title: Retouching refinements and color-control philosophy
sections.description: A deeper dive into tonal-based color adjustments, color calibration, and a blue-gold filter discussion. The technique emphasizes keeping skies recolored via tonal adjustments rather than direct color paints, plus the use of the 50-150 selective color approach to energize specific tonal ranges in the scene.

sections.title: Final passes, black-and-white detours, and wrap
sections.description: The final segments compare color-rich processing with selective black-and-white iterations, including a discussion on the Orton diffusion, and a demonstration of the clone-paint/history-paint approaches for multi-shot consistency. The wrap emphasizes choosing sky and composition strategically, preserving horizon lines, and the value of saving layered histories for future revisits.
